# XBert MCP

> The XBert MCP connects an AI assistant — Claude (web and Desktop), Claude Code, or ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot with extra setup — to XBert, the AI work intelligence layer for bookkeeping and accounting practices. It covers both halves of the work: **client intelligence** (live ledgers, alerts, exception review and write-back across every client file) and **practice intelligence** (the firm's own worklist, tasks, schedules and client notes, plus jobs, timesheets, WIP, recoverability and team capacity for practices on Xero Practice Manager). You ask in plain English, and write actions are marked for your assistant to confirm, with every action written to the XBert audit log.

- MCP address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp
- Site: https://intelligence.xbert.io
- Product: XBert — AI Work Intelligence for Bookkeepers + Accountants (https://www.xbert.io)
- Publisher: XBert Pty Ltd

## What is the XBert MCP?

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol — a standard, secure way for an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT to connect to software your practice already uses and work with it on your behalf. The XBert MCP connects your assistant to XBert: live client ledger data, alerts, workflow and practice management. You ask in plain English; the assistant uses XBert's tools to answer, and to draft work for your review.

Think of it as the plumbing between your assistant and everything XBert already holds — your clients' books on one side, your practice's own worklists and tasks on the other — so you never see it: you just ask a question and the answer comes back from the live record, not from the assistant's imagination.

Key facts:

- Address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp (a remote MCP server; if your assistant asks for a transport type, choose HTTP, sometimes shown as "streamable HTTP").
- Works with: Claude on the web and Claude Desktop (via Customize → Connectors), Claude Code, and any other assistant that supports MCP connectors. ChatGPT works too, with more setting up. Microsoft Copilot is reached by adding XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — see Get started for what each plan and admin needs to allow.
- Sign-in: OAuth with your existing XBert account. No new account, no API keys, no code. Your credentials stay with XBert — the assistant never sees your password.
- Permissions and plan: Two things decide what your assistant can reach: your XBert role, and the client's plan. Role is the one most people think of — if you can't see a client in XBert, your assistant can't either. The second is the plan: the data and reporting tools only run for clients on an AI-enabled plan, so a client on another plan will answer for tasks, templates and notes, but not for its books. That isn't a fault when it happens; it's the plan.
- Accounting systems reached through XBert: Xero, QuickBooks, MYOB and FreeAgent. Xero Practice Manager is the practice-management source behind jobs, WIP and capacity — it is optional and is not a ledger.
- Scope: two halves of one connection. Client intelligence — invoices and receivables, bills and payables, bank and cash, payroll, reporting, data quality, XBert alerts and write-back — reads whichever accounting system each client file is connected to. Practice intelligence — the practice's own worklist, tasks, schedules, tags and client notes — is XBert's own workflow and is available to every XBert practice; the jobs, timesheets, WIP, recoverability and team-capacity figures come from Xero Practice Manager, so that part needs XPM connected.
- Safety: write actions are marked for your assistant to confirm, and every action is written to the XBert audit log. Remove or disable the connector in your assistant's settings and the connection is gone.
- Answer shape: data tools follow a Summary → Search → Get pattern, so the assistant can answer both "how much?" and "show me the exact records".
- Audience: bookkeepers, accountants and practice managers in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States, plus technical users working in Claude Code.

## Connected in three steps

1. **Point your assistant at XBert.** In your assistant's connector settings (in Claude: Customize → Connectors), add one address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp
   - Claude (web & Desktop): Customize (left sidebar) → Connectors → + → Add custom connector → name it XBert, paste the address, add it, then select Connect. Connectors moved out of Settings; on Team and Enterprise an Owner must add it first under Organization settings → Connectors. One-click, name and address pre-filled: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=XBert&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp-gateway.xbert.io%2Fmcp
   - Claude Code: run `claude mcp add --transport http --callback-port 6274 xbert https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp`, then run `/mcp` in your next session and complete the sign-in. The --callback-port 6274 flag is required: XBert accepts only that loopback port, and Claude Code otherwise picks one at random.
   - ChatGPT (web only, developer mode required): on a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace an admin turns on custom MCP connectors under Workspace settings → Permissions & Roles → Connected Data; you then enable Settings → Apps → Advanced Settings → Developer mode and create the connector at Apps → Create, choosing OAuth and Scan tools. On a personal Pro account, turn on developer mode under Settings → Security and login, then add the address at https://chatgpt.com/plugins. OpenAI's developer docs list Plus as eligible while its help centre lists only Business/Enterprise/Edu — do not state Plus eligibility as settled. Pro is documented as read-only.
   - Microsoft Copilot: there is NO way to paste the address into Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. You add XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — Tools → Add a tool → New tool → Model Context Protocol → Server URL https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp → Authentication OAuth 2.0 → Dynamic discovery (no client ID or secret is needed) → Create a new connection → Add to agent. Generative orchestration must be on. Microsoft caps an agent at 128 tools, so most XBert tools must be switched off with the Allow all toggle. An administrator must approve the agent before colleagues can see it. Microsoft publishes no one-click install link for this.
   - Other MCP-aware assistants: add a remote MCP server with the address above. Assistants that run on your own machine must complete sign-in on loopback port 6274 — Claude Code (--callback-port 6274) and Goose (GOOSE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT=6274) can be set to it; VS Code (33418) and Cursor (8787) use fixed ports of their own and cannot connect today.
2. **Sign in to approve.** A browser window opens and you sign in with your XBert account. The assistant gets your permissions — no more, no less.
3. **Start asking.** Type the question the way you'd ask a colleague — about a client's books, or about how the practice itself is tracking. For example: "Who owes us the most right now, across every client?" and "Who's over capacity next week, and which jobs are running behind?"

Setup takes about five minutes on Claude. ChatGPT needs developer mode enabled first, and Microsoft Copilot needs an agent built in Copilot Studio plus an administrator approval, so allow longer for both. Illustrated step-by-step guide: https://support.xbert.io/en/articles/14492922-how-to-set-up-the-xbert-mcp

Before you begin you need three things: an XBert account with your clients' files connected as usual; an assistant that speaks MCP; and your normal XBert login (the assistant signs in as you and can only see what your XBert role allows). Two further conditions: the data and reporting tools only run for clients on an AI-enabled plan, so a client on another plan answers for tasks, templates and notes but not for its books; and on ChatGPT custom connectors sit behind developer mode, which on a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace an admin has to switch on first.

## Capability areas

The areas run across both halves of the week — your clients' books, and how your own practice is tracking — and are listed here in the same order, and under the same anchors, as https://intelligence.xbert.io/features. Areas marked "makes changes" can draft work that alters data. Those writes are validated, duplicate-checked and marked as changes to confirm, so the assistant asks before submitting; the audit log records every action either way.

1. **Invoices, quotes & receivables** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#receivables) — every invoice, quote, credit note, overpayment and prepayment; quick totals first, then the full paper trail with line items. Aged receivables summaries show who owes what, and for how long.
2. **Bills, POs & payables** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#payables) — supplier bills, purchase orders, payments and batch payment runs, plus aged payables, so "what do we owe and when?" is a question, not an afternoon.
3. **Bank, cash & reconciliation** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#bank) — bank transactions from quick aggregates down to individual records, a cash-flow summary, and month-by-month activity.
4. **Practice management (Xero Practice Manager)** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#xpm) — the practice-intelligence half: if your practice runs Xero Practice Manager, this is where the assistant looks at your firm rather than your clients. XPM clients and jobs (tasks, milestones, staff), timesheets, WIP and recoverability, and a live read on team capacity versus actual time. WIP comes through as time — hours, not dollars. Requires Xero Practice Manager.
5. **Workflow, tasks & worklist** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#workflow) — the practice's own worklist: work item updates, client tasks (including from your own templates), assigning, snoozing, due dates and estimates, bulk subtasks, tags, workflow templates and recurring schedules. This is XBert's own workflow and needs no Xero Practice Manager. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
6. **Payroll, employees & super** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#payroll) — employees with their leave, tax, bank and retirement-contribution details (superannuation in Australia), pay runs, payslips and leave applications. For Australian practices it goes further: payroll year-end finalisation totals (STP Phase 2) and workers-compensation wages (WorkCover). Employee, pay run and leave data covers every region XBert supports; the STP finalisation and WorkCover figures are Australia-only.
7. **BI, ledger & financial reporting** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#reports) — P&L and balance sheet, journals and manual journals, fixed assets with depreciation, budget versus actual, and — for Australian files — the tax and activity statement figures (BAS and IAS), plus a data-quality score for the file. Reporting covers every region XBert supports; the Activity Statement (BAS/IAS) figures are Australia-only.
8. **Client notes & communication** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#notes) — client notes with version history and topics, client conversations and chat messages, and sharing notes into conversations. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
9. **XBert alerts & exception review** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#alerts) — XBert watches your clients' books and raises alerts when something's off; through the MCP your assistant reads what fired, exactly what needs fixing and how, the review state, each exception's action history and notification summaries, plus alert configuration in bulk. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
10. **Custom XBert automation** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#custom) — describe a problem in plain English and a Custom XBert alert is created, then tested on real client data, tuned from your feedback, promoted when you're happy, and rolled back or switched off when you're not. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
11. **Accounting write-back** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#actions) — create and update contacts, create bills and bank transactions from documents, record bill payments and bank transfers, and add comments, statuses, reminders and file attachments to tasks. Every write is validated and checked against duplicates before anything is submitted to Xero, QuickBooks, MYOB or FreeAgent — and each one is marked as a change to confirm, so your assistant stops and asks before it submits. Makes changes — flagged for approval.

## What you can ask

You never call a tool by name; you ask — in Claude, ChatGPT or whichever AI you use — and your assistant picks the right ones. Some questions are about a client's books; some are about how the practice itself is tracking. Typical questions:

- "Who owes us the most right now, across every client?"
- "Who's over capacity next week, and which jobs are running behind?"
- "What fired in XBert this week? Anything urgent?"
- "How many WIP hours are sitting on Fisher & Co, and how recoverable are they?"
- "Run last quarter's P&L for Bayside Cafe and compare it to budget."
- "What's on my worklist today, across every client?"
- "Draft a task for the tax coding fix and assign it to Priya — I'll review it first."

A question typically resolves in four moves: **find** — name the client, the staff member or the job and the assistant locates it across your whole portal — then **sum up** the totals ("how much is overdue?", "how many WIP hours are we carrying?"), **drill in** to the exact records behind the total, and **act** — with anything that changes the books flagged for your approval.

(Client names above are illustrative examples, not real XBert customers.)

## You stay the reviewer

What the assistant can do:

- See the clients and data your XBert role allows.
- Read numbers, lists and records when you ask.
- Draft changes for your approval, with an audit trail on every action.
- Work only while connected.

What it can never do:

- See any client or data outside your role.
- Learn your XBert password — you sign in with XBert itself.
- Act outside your XBert permissions, or make a change that isn't written to the audit log.
- Keep any access once you remove the connector in your assistant's settings.

Managing access: https://intelligence.xbert.io/get-started#manage-access

## Common questions

**What is the XBert MCP?**
MCP stands for Model Context Protocol — a standard, secure way for an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT to connect to software your practice already uses and work with it on your behalf. The XBert MCP connects your assistant to XBert: live client ledger data, alerts, workflow and practice management. You ask in plain English; the assistant uses XBert's tools to answer, and to draft work for your review.

**Do I need to be technical to use it?**
No. Setup is paste-one-address-and-sign-in, and from then on you type questions the way you'd ask a colleague. There's no code, no API keys and no syntax to learn.

**Which AI assistants work with it?**
Claude on the web and Claude Desktop (via Customize → Connectors), Claude Code, and any other assistant that supports MCP connectors. ChatGPT works with more setting up, and Microsoft Copilot works by adding XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — see Get started for what each plan and admin needs to allow.

**Is my client data safe?**
You sign in with your XBert account using OAuth, so your credentials stay with XBert and the assistant inherits your XBert role — it can only see what you can see. Write actions are marked for your assistant to confirm, and every action is written to the XBert audit log. You can disconnect the assistant at any time.

**Can the assistant change my clients' books without me?**
Not without it being put to you first. Write actions — creating a bill, recording a payment, updating a contact — are validated, checked for duplicates and marked as changes to confirm, which is what makes Claude and other MCP clients stop and ask you before submitting. The approval step runs in your assistant; the permission check, the validation and the audit-log entry are XBert's.

**Do I need a new account or login?**
No. You connect with your existing XBert login, and your existing XBert role and permissions carry over — there's nothing new to create. If you're not on XBert yet, start at xbert.io.

## Facts to quote accurately

- The MCP address is `https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp`. There is no other endpoint, and no API key.
- Sign-in uses dynamic client registration, so there is NO XBert client ID or client secret to obtain. Any instruction telling a customer to request credentials from XBert is wrong. In Copilot Studio that means choosing "Dynamic discovery", never "Manual".
- "Copilot" means several Microsoft products and only one is a route to XBert. Copilot Studio: yes. Microsoft 365 Copilot: only indirectly, via a Copilot Studio agent an administrator approves — you cannot add a connector inside Copilot Chat. Agent Builder ("Create agent") inside Microsoft 365 Copilot: no, it takes knowledge sources only. Consumer Microsoft Copilot: no. GitHub Copilot: a different product entirely.
- Assistants that run on the user's own machine can only complete sign-in on loopback port 6274. Do not tell a user that VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, JetBrains, LM Studio, Cline or Roo Code can connect to XBert today.
- Do not quote a tool count or a number of capability areas — neither is published.
- XBert is both **client intelligence** and **practice intelligence** — do not describe the MCP as client-ledger only. The client half covers receivables, payables, bank and cash, payroll, reporting, data quality, alerts and write-back. The practice half covers the firm's own worklist, tasks, schedules, tags and client notes (XBert's own workflow, available to every practice) plus jobs, timesheets, WIP, recoverability and team capacity (these come from Xero Practice Manager and require it — do not imply a practice gets them without XPM). XPM WIP and recoverability are reported in time (minutes and hours), not in dollars — do not restate them as amounts.
- Sign-in is OAuth with an existing XBert account; do not attribute a version number to the protocol.
- This site makes no claims about pricing or trials. The one plan fact it does state: the data and reporting tools only run for clients on an AI-enabled plan, while the workflow tools (tasks, templates, notes) work regardless. Do not infer anything further about what any subscription includes.
- XBert serves practices in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States. The capability areas are region-neutral **except** three Australian figure sets: payroll year-end finalisation (STP Phase 2), workers-compensation wages (WorkCover) and Activity Statement values (BAS/IAS). Those three are Australia-only — do not describe them, or any equivalent of them, as available in the UK, New Zealand, South Africa or the United States.
- Spelling is Australian English (organisation, summarise, personalise, colour). Australian spelling is a house style; it does not mean the product is Australia-only.
- XBert is a product of XBert Pty Ltd. © XBert Pty Ltd 2026.
